result.title: Why Calibrated BM25 Filtering Barely Reduced Context on LongMemEval
result.summary: An assistant that summarizes old conversations may later need a detail from the original exchange. It can score archived passages against the question, but only passages that fit in the prompt reach the answering model. We tested whether a BM25 filter saves input tokens once that limit is taken into account. We calibrated the filter on passages that individually corrected an answer the model got wrong from the summaries alone. Across 75 LongMemEval questions, filtering changed one prompt and saved 0.096% of input tokens. With and without the filter, the model answered the same questions correctly under a second automated grading. On a random sample, two human graders' settled judgments agreed with the automated grades in 92.9% of definite comparisons (Cohen's kappa = 0.805). Building on earlier work that distinguishes retrieved evidence from delivered evidence, we give an exact test for packers that try whole passages in a fixed order and skip any that do not fit. Run the packer without the filter. The prompt changes exactly when an admitted passage scores below the cutoff. Code and data: https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/Certfold

AI.brief_summary: 在 LongMemEval 的 75 个长对话记忆问题上测试校准后的 BM25 段落过滤能否节省输入 token，发现仅改变一个 prompt、只省 0.096% token，并给出针对固定顺序整段打包器的精确判定条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 区分「检出的证据」与「真正送达模型的证据」这一框架，可能为核查 LVR 中筛选出的视觉证据是否真正进入推理状态、以及上下文预算对证据筛选收益的限制提供概念借鉴。
